SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK FP-09: FHIRPath — §5.6.1-§5.6.5 String Manipulation (Search). Test these items: indexOf(substring), substring(start, [length]), startsWith(prefix), endsWith(suffix), contains(substring). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.evidence: Fresh FP-09 EXPLORER probe found forced Python fallback fhirpath_is_valid() mismatches against native C++ for literal-union string-search arguments. Native returned false for s.substring((1|2)) and s.substring(1,(1|2)); fallback returned true even though substring start/length are singleton Integer parameters and (1|2) has two distinct items. Native returned true for s.indexOf(('a'|'a')); fallback returned false even though union eliminates duplicates and leaves one String argument. Before-fix log: .temp/qa/fp09_explorer_probe_before_fix.log.
issues.root_cause: The forced Python fallback fhirpath_is_valid() FP-09 static precheck used masked token heuristics for literal unions. It treated every string-literal union as invalid because it could not distinguish duplicate-eliminated singleton unions, and it did not evaluate literal Integer unions for substring start/length arguments.
issues.resolution: Added position-preserving function-call argument scanning for FP-09 validation, parsed simple literal union arguments, applied union duplicate elimination including numeric equality while preserving the first effective item type, and validated the effective singleton item type for string-search parameters. Added native/fallback regression coverage for duplicate and multi-item literal-union arguments.
